q: Martin-Löf randomness for an infinite sequence x ∈ {0,1}^ω is defined using effective null sets. Equivalently, x is Martin-Löf random iff:
opts: The prefix-free complexity K(xₙ) of the first n bits satisfies K(xₙ) ≥ n − O(1)
x is generated by a fair coin
exp: By the Schnorr-Levin theorem, Martin-Löf randomness ↔ K(xₙ) ≥ n − c for some constant c (all n). Sequences failing this have compressible initial segments and are non-random.
